best_for: Windows developers who want the official Go toolchain from an MSI, or who need to pin an older Go release to match a project or CI build.

points.title: The official toolchain, free
points.text: This is the Go compiler, standard library and `go` command from the Go project, under a BSD-style license. There is no account and no paid tier; editors and IDEs sit on top of it.

points.title: An MSI for each Windows chip
points.text: The project ships MSI installers for 32-bit x86, x64 and Arm64, all installing for every user on the machine, so they need administrator rights. Zip archives exist too if you would rather unpack without installing.

points.title: Windows 10 or later
points.text: The download page lists Windows 10 or later for the x64 MSI. If you are on an older Windows, you need an older Go release.

points.title: Only two releases get fixes
points.text: Each major release is supported until two newer ones are out, with security fixes shipped as point releases. Go 1.27 came out in August 2026, and 1.27.4 in November carried security fixes to cgo, the linker and `net/http`.

points.title: Old versions for reproducible builds
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 115 versions, which helps when a project pins a specific Go release. Unsupported releases no longer receive security fixes, so use them for builds, not for new work.

points.title: Mac and Linux come from go.dev
points.text: This listing covers Windows only. The Go project offers .pkg installers for Intel and Apple silicon Macs that need macOS 13 or later, and Linux tarballs for x64, Arm64 and several other chips.
